name: llm-judge
description: The ticket 11.5 canonical llm_judge workflow (ADR-013/ADR-012). A `draft` llm step carries a validation chain naming the cost-bearing `llm_judge` validator: a cheap judge model grades the draft against a rubric and passes only when its score meets the threshold. The judge is the last link in the chain (cheap-first ordering means it runs only on an output the free validators already accepted); a below-threshold verdict carries the judge's rationale, which the `feedback` template folds into the next semantic attempt's prompt, so the draft self-corrects. The judge's provider call is attributed to the `draft` step as OVERHEAD (ADR-012 rule 4) — it appears in `GET /v1/runs/{id}/cost` as a `judge:*` entry with `overhead: true` and in the per-step `overhead_nano_usd` roll-up, separate from the draft's own productive spend. `on_error: skip` degrades to a pass with a warning when the judge provider is unavailable, so an outage never blocks the workflow. Judges are terminal — a judge's output is never itself validated or judged. It runs against the offline mock provider (models `mock/sim-1` and `mock/judge-1`); swapping the model ids for real providers makes it a live semantic quality gate unchanged.

config.prompt: Write a concise, well-supported answer to the user's question and cite a source.

config.rubric: Score 1 if the answer is detailed and cites a source; score 0 if it is terse or unsupported.
